title: Insecure Direct Object Reference in POST /api/bookings
description: The seat reservation route permitted unauthenticated or unauthorized callers to create bookings on behalf of any arbitrary student identifier without validating token identity ownership.
root_cause: The route extracted studentId directly from the request JSON body and issued seat reservations without verifying that the caller was authenticated or authorized to act on behalf of that student.
intended_behavior: Enforce verified JWT session authentication and confirm that studentId matches the caller's session.userId or session.studentId unless caller possesses admin or staff privileges.
remediation: Implemented getSessionFromRequest(req) validation and explicit session ownership cross-checking in src/app/api/bookings/route.ts.

title: Unauthenticated Booking Cancellation via POST /api/bookings/cancel
description: Any caller could cancel arbitrary passenger seat reservations across the entire fleet by supplying a booking ID without demonstrating booking ownership.
root_cause: The cancellation handler updated the booking record status to CANCELLED without checking caller session credentials or ownership.
intended_behavior: Verify that the cancellation requester is authenticated and either owns the reservation or holds transport management / staff credentials.
remediation: Added session authentication and strict ownership verification matching booking.student_id against session.userId.

title: Privilege Escalation via Client-Supplied performedByStaff in /api/students/profile
description: Clients could bypass administrative field editing controls by supplying performedByStaff: true in the request body.
root_cause: The handler used Boolean(body.performedByStaff) as part of isStaffOrAdmin evaluation instead of relying strictly on verified server JWT claims.
intended_behavior: Evaluate administrative and staff permissions exclusively through cryptographically verified session.role claims.
remediation: Removed body.performedByStaff and bound elevated access checks strictly to session.role.

title: Missing HTTP Security Defense Headers
description: The Next.js configuration lacked critical baseline HTTP headers (HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), exposing the application to clickjacking and MIME confusion.
root_cause: No custom security headers were declared in next.config.mjs.
intended_behavior: Declare modern standard HTTP defensive headers for all route responses.
remediation: Configured Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy in next.config.mjs.
